title: Washing Day
story: On Sunday Elena carried a basket of wet clothes down to the courtyard. The sun was out, and the washing line was free. She shook each shirt and hung it with a wooden peg. A blue shirt belonged to her brother Hugo. A white towel belonged to her. The wind was light, so the clothes moved but did not fall. At noon a cloud covered the sun. Elena looked up and decided to wait. Ten minutes later the cloud passed. She turned the shirts so the other side could dry. Her neighbour Ines came out with her own basket and asked if there was room. Elena moved the towel along the line and made a space. Ines thanked her and hung two pillowcases. They talked about the weather while they worked. By four o'clock the clothes were dry. Elena folded them into the basket and took the pegs off the line. She left the line clear for the next person. Upstairs, Hugo looked for his blue shirt and found it on the chair, warm and smooth. Elena put the pegs in a tin so they would not get lost. The courtyard was empty again, and the line moved gently in the wind.
